newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Alliance says won't give Labour blank cheque.
newsitem.headline: NZ Alliance says won't give Labour blank cheque.

text.p: Alliance leader Jim Anderton said on Saturday there was no guarantee the Alliance would support a left-wing coalition, and his party would require a written response to the initiatives it wanted to see in place.

"If Labour and New Zealand First need the Alliance to govern, and they think there is some kind of blank cheque or footstool position here, that they can just do anything they like, I will remind them that we were elected on a platform of promises and commitments that we said we would honour," he told TV3.

"If they don't show any inclination to deliver the kind of programmes that we have pledged to our supporters, there is no reason for the Alliance to vote for parties that think they can arrogantly ride roughshod over the wishes of a significant number of New Zealanders."

The left-wing Alliance is projected to win about 13 seats in the 120-member parliament. Its support would be enough to allow Labour (36 projected seats) and nationalist New Zealand First (17) to form a government.
Anderton said the party had drafted a paper of initiatives on which it would require a written response from any party that wanted the Alliance's support in government.
The final draft would be discussed on Sunday before the Alliance caucus approved it on Tuesday.
"Then we'll have it in the hands of any party leader that thinks they can form a government, apart from National, who we are not interested in going into coalition with," Anderton said.
He said many people who voted for Labour and New Zealand First probably believed those parties would carry out many of the initiatives the Alliance stood for.

"When we put to them a wish to confirm that, and to respond to some of the extensions of policy that I think many New Zealanders would like to see anyway, if they just toss it out willy nilly they are taking a huge risk with their own support base." he said.
Anderton also said he did not believe New Zealand First was a centre-left party in the first instance.
"If you look at their policies, they actually balance out much easier with National than with Labour or the Alliance...
"There may actually be a right wing coalition, and I believe that if New Zealand First joints National that's what they'll show themselves to be."
